## 3. Scorecard

Ratings are my judgment against the evidence in this report. "Strong" means implemented and checked here; "Adequate" means present with material caveats; "Weak" means present but insufficient for the claim; "Absent" means not implemented.

| Dimension | Rating | Evidence | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|---|
| Isolation and determinism | **Strong** | Fresh home/ws/tmp; telemetry off; no LLM judge; fixed question ids and model rule (`README.md:9,13`; `run.mjs:63-79,165-199`) | Removes the largest sources of accidental variance |
| Scoring transparency | **Strong** | Scorer is open code; every metric has a named implementation | Readers can audit what the number means |
| Failure accounting | **Adequate** | Timeouts/exit codes/refusals recorded; but `done` conflates process with quality; the catch-all error row loses most fields (`run.mjs:285`) | Prevents silent success, but not silent degradation |
| Raw provenance | **Weak** | Metadata is good, but `workdir` is an absolute author-local path; no artifacts are committed; `--rescore` cannot work from a clone (`run.mjs:267-274`; result rows) | A result file is a receipt, not a reproduction |
| Construct validity | **Weak** | Metrics cover citation existence/title overlap/key-paper presence; no claim support, synthesis quality, source quality, or research decision | The measured construct is narrower than "research quality" |
| Statistical power | **Weak** | 4 questions per run, one run per condition, no repeats or intervals; 4/4 completion has a 95% Wilson interval of roughly [0.51, 1.0] | 100% on n=4 is not a 100% capability claim |
| Coverage | **Weak** | 4 of 12 questions have committed results; only `/lit` in committed results; `/deepresearch` wired but unused; `/audit`, `/review`, `/replicate`, `/recipe`, `/compare`, `/draft`, `/summarize` unmeasured | Most of the product's research surface is unevaluated |
| Contamination control | **Absent** | Questions use canonical papers (test-time compute, speculative decoding, CRISPR base editing, etc.); no no-tool baseline, no post-cutoff set, no perturbation control | Recall can measure memorization as much as retrieval |
| Meta-evaluation | **Weak** | No tests reference `evals/`; CI does not run it; no adversarial fixtures or human audit | The scorer's failure modes are unknown until someone probes them |
| Process adherence | **Weak** | Rule requires before/after runs for prompt/tool/Pi changes; 110 commits touched those paths since 2026-09-24; 0 commits touched `evals/`; no eval result after that date | A voluntary gate that is not run is not a gate |
| Cost and latency | **Adequate** | Wall time and tokens measured; all 22 rows show `cost_usd = 0`, and the documented example `models.json` has no `cost` block | Token counts are useful; dollar cost is not being measured |
| Privacy and ethics | **Strong** | Isolated homes; telemetry off; keys env-only; content-free telemetry in the product | Research artifacts can be sensitive; this is handled well |
| Documentation honesty | **Strong** | README caveats, known issues, refusal disclosures, explicit "single run is noisy" | Readers are warned about the main limitations |

content.text:
# Feynman eval-scorer probe

Synthetic-artifact meta-evaluation of `evals/run.mjs` from
[Companion-Inc/feynman](https://github.com/Companion-Inc/feynman) at commit
`11744290758648c2ecd7c0d6389cdca9ae580290` (package 0.5.69, 2026-11-13).

The point is to test the scorer, not the model: each case is a hand-written
`outputs/<slug>.md` plus (sometimes) a provenance sidecar. The scorer is run
with `--rescore`, exactly as the repo documents.

## Reproduce

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/Companion-Inc/feynman.git /tmp/feynman-src
python3 make_fixtures.py
cd /tmp/feynman-src
node evals/run.mjs --rescore /work/experiments/feynman-eval-audit/fixtures.jsonl
```

`--rescore` rewrites the input JSONL in place with score fields and writes
`fixtures.md` next to it. The scored output is committed here as
`fixtures.jsonl` / `fixtures.md`; raw stdout is in `rescore.log`.

## Cases (all use `q01`, test-time compute scaling)

| id | artifact content | expected probe |
|---|---|---|
| `f1-control` | correct claim + correct paper, arXiv URL, exact title | all metrics pass |
| `f2-fake-id` | exact title, fabricated arXiv ID `2408.99999` | `valid` fails, `recall` still passes |
| `f3-irrelevant` | real paper, exact title, unrelated topic | `valid`/`title` pass, `recall` fails |
| `f4-absurd-number` | "improves MATH accuracy by 1000%" + correct citation | all metrics pass |
| `f5-wrong-title` | correct ID, wrong bracketed title, claim text repeats title words | `title` still passes |
| `f6-no-provenance` | correct artifact, no `.provenance.md` sidecar | `done` fails |
| `f7-bare-id` | bare ID `2408.03314`, no exact title, no URL/prefix | `cites` = 0, `recall` = 100% |
| `f8-rejected` | key paper only in a "Rejected sources" list | `recall` = 100% |

## Results

See `fixtures.md` for the generated table and `fixtures.jsonl` for per-case
fields. Summary:

| case | done | cites | valid | title | recall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| f1-control | yes | 1 | 100% | 100% | 100% |
| f2-fake-id | yes | 1 | 0% | - | 100% |
| f3-irrelevant | yes | 1 | 100% | 100% | 0% |
| f4-absurd-number | yes | 1 | 100% | 100% | 100% |
| f5-wrong-title | yes | 1 | 100% | 100% | 100% |
| f6-no-provenance | no | 0 | - | - | 0% |
| f7-bare-id | yes | 0 | - | - | 100% |
| f8-rejected | yes | 1 | 100% | 100% | 100% |

All results are deterministic given the same fixture text and live
arXiv/Crossref responses. Network lookups were available for these runs.

## What this does and does not show

- It confirms documented scope limits: relevance is not checked by
  `valid`/`title`; numeric claims are not checked at all; and recall is string
  presence, not use. The undocumented findings are the title heuristic
  false-positive (surrounding prose satisfies it) and the `cites`/`recall`
  inconsistency for bare IDs. It also shows the process-only `done` gate.
- It does **not** show that any committed model run contains these errors.
  The committed result files do not include the artifacts, so their 44
  citations cannot be inspected from the repo.

## 3. Scorecard

Ratings are my judgment against the evidence in this report. "Strong" means implemented and checked here; "Adequate" means present with material caveats; "Weak" means present but insufficient for the claim; "Absent" means not implemented.

| Dimension | Rating | Evidence | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|---|
| Isolation | **Strong** | Fresh home/ws/tmp; telemetry off; fixed question ids and model rule (`README.md:9,13`; `run.mjs:63-79`) | Removes the largest sources of accidental variance |
| Scoring logic determinism | **Strong** | No LLM judge; same artifact text and lookup outcomes produce the same score (`run.mjs:165-199`) | The scorer is auditable and repeatable |
| Measurement stability | **Adequate** | `valid` drops network-failed lookups from the denominator (`run.mjs:183`; `README.md:48`); pre-wait q01 was manually re-scored after a transient lookup failure | `valid` is conditional on lookup success, not artifact-only |
| Scoring transparency | **Strong** | Scorer is open code; every metric has a named implementation | Readers can audit what the number means |
| Failure accounting | **Adequate** | Timeouts/exit codes/refusals recorded; but `done` conflates process with quality; the catch-all error row loses most fields (`run.mjs:285`) | Prevents silent success, but not silent degradation |
| Raw provenance | **Weak** | Metadata is good, but `workdir` is an absolute author-local path; no artifacts are committed; `--rescore` cannot work from a clone (`run.mjs:267-274`; result rows) | A result file is a receipt, not a reproduction |
| Construct validity | **Weak** | Metrics cover citation existence/title overlap/key-paper presence; no claim support, synthesis quality, source quality, or research decision | The measured construct is narrower than "research quality" |
| Statistical power | **Weak** | 2–4 questions per run (one Opus run has 2 after biology refusals), one run per condition, no repeats or intervals; 4/4 completion has a 95% Wilson interval of roughly [0.51, 1.0] | 100% on n=4 is not a 100% capability claim |
| Coverage | **Weak** | 4 of 12 questions have committed results; only `/lit` in committed results; `/deepresearch` wired but unused; `/audit`, `/review`, `/replicate`, `/recipe`, `/compare`, `/draft`, `/summarize` unmeasured | Most of the product's research surface is unevaluated |
| Contamination control | **Absent** | Questions use canonical papers (test-time compute, speculative decoding, CRISPR base editing, etc.); no no-tool baseline, no post-cutoff set, no perturbation control | Recall can measure memorization as much as retrieval |
| Meta-evaluation | **Weak** | No tests reference `evals/`; CI does not run it; no adversarial fixtures or human audit | The scorer's failure modes are unknown until someone probes them |
| Process adherence | **Weak** | Rule requires before/after runs for prompt/tool/Pi changes; 46 substantive commits touched prompts/agents/skills/extensions since 2026-09-24 (110 including `package.json` release/version commits); 0 commits touched `evals/`; no eval result after that date | A voluntary gate that is not run is not a gate |
| Cost and latency | **Adequate** | Wall time and tokens measured; all 22 rows show `cost_usd = 0`, and the documented example `models.json` has no `cost` block | Token counts are useful; dollar cost is not being measured |
| Privacy and ethics | **Strong** | Isolated homes; telemetry off; keys env-only; content-free telemetry in the product | Research artifacts can be sensitive; this is handled well |
| Documentation honesty | **Strong** | README caveats, known issues, refusal disclosures, explicit "single run is noisy" | Readers are warned about the main limitations |

**Overall:** the infrastructure is solid; the measurement is narrower than the claims; the operating discipline has decayed. A fair one-line summary is: *good smoke test, not yet a benchmark.*
---
| Case | Artifact content | `done` | `valid` | `title` | `recall` | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| f1-control | Correct claim + correct paper, URL, exact title | yes | 100% | 100% | 100% | All four surface metrics pass with no workflow |
| f2-fake-id | Exact title, fabricated ID `2408.99999` | yes | 0% | – | 100% | `recall` is title string presence, not resolvability |
| f3-irrelevant | Real paper, exact title, unrelated topic | yes | 100% | 100% | 0% | `valid`/`title` do not measure relevance |
| f4-absurd-number | "Improves MATH accuracy by 1000%" + correct citation | yes | 100% | 100% | 100% | No numeric or claim-support check |
| f5-wrong-title | Correct ID, wrong bracketed title, claim text repeats title words | yes | 100% | 100% | 100% | Title heuristic satisfied by surrounding prose (8/11 title tokens, 72.7%) |
| f6-no-provenance | Correct artifact, no sidecar | no | – | – | 0% | `done` is filename existence; process gate works |
| f7-bare-id | Bare `2408.03314`, no exact key-paper title | yes | – | – | 100% | `cites` misses bare IDs; `keyRecall`'s raw substring sees the ID |
| f8-rejected | Key paper only in a "Rejected sources" list | yes | 100% | 100% | 100% | Recall credits presence, not use |

Raw scores: `experiments/feynman-eval-audit/fixtures.jsonl`, `fixtures.md`, `rescore.log`.

Most of these results confirm limits the README already states (identifier resolution, title overlap, presence-based recall). The undocumented findings are the title-heuristic false positive (`f5`) and the `cites`/`recall` extraction inconsistency (`f7`).

### What the probe establishes

1. **A synthetic one-paragraph artifact scores 100%.** `f1-control` has one sentence and a minimal provenance file. It passes `done`, `valid`, `title`, and `recall`. The scorer cannot distinguish it from a six-stage `/lit` run. This is expected from an outcome-based eval, but it means a perfect score is compatible with no research process at all.
2. **The title check has a false-positive mode.** `f5-wrong-title` attaches the title "Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models" to the correct ID for the test-time-compute paper. The line also contains the claim "test-time compute can be scaled more effectively than model parameters." Because the scorer compares the resolved title to the whole line, 8 of 11 title tokens overlap (72.7% ≥ 60%), so `title` passes. The README warns about short-name citations missing; it does not warn about prose satisfying the check.
3. **Recall is presence, not use.** `f2-fake-id` gets 100% recall with a fabricated ID because the exact title is present. `f8-rejected` gets 100% recall because the paper appears in a rejected-sources list. A report could "recall" every key paper while excluding it from the synthesis.
4. **There is no claim-level check.** `f4-absurd-number` claims a 1000% accuracy improvement and cites the correct paper. All four metrics pass. Identifier resolution and title overlap say nothing about whether the cited paper supports the sentence.
5. **`done` is a process gate only.** `f6-no-provenance` fails because the sidecar is missing; `f1-control` passes with a minimal sidecar that contains no real provenance. The metric checks existence, not content.
6. **Extraction is format-sensitive.** `f7-bare-id` contains the bare ID `2408.03314` and no exact key-paper title. `cites` is 0 because `extractIds` requires a URL or `arxiv:` prefix, but `recall` is 100% because `keyRecall` does a raw substring match on the text. The same paper is simultaneously uncounted and counted.

These are not exotic adversarial cases. Wrong-but-resolvable citations, rejected sources, bare IDs, and unsupported numbers are ordinary failure modes in research writing. The eval's own README is honest that it measures citation resolution rather than truth; the risk is that the summary table and release prose invite a stronger reading.

---

## 5. Release-claim audit

The most specific public claim is in `RELEASES.md` for v0.5.3 (2026-09-24):

> "On the `/lit` eval with GPT-5.6 Terra, 4 of 4 questions finished, all 44 citations resolved with matching titles, and each question ran the researcher, verifier, and reviewer in under 11 minutes (0.5.2: 9-14 minutes, 43 of 43 citations)."

| Claim | Check | Result | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 of 4 questions finished | Read the 0.5.3 Terra JSONL | 4/4 `completed: true` | Recomputed, consistent |
| 44 citations | Sum `citations` across q01/q04/q07/q10 | 11 + 11 + 7 + 15 = 44 distinct identifiers | Recomputed, consistent |
| All 44 resolved | `citations_checked` = 44; all `citation_validity` = 1 | 44/44 | Recomputed, consistent |
| `valid` is artifact-only | Read `run.mjs:183` and the pre-wait summaries | Network-failed lookups are dropped from the denominator; q01 was manually re-scored after a transient failure | **Conditional on lookup success** |
| Matching titles | Every row's `title_match` = 1 | All rows pass the 60% heuristic; the denominator is resolved IDs with a known title, not necessarily all 44 | Recomputed, but heuristic-dependent |
| Under 11 minutes each | `wall_s` = 652, 628, 578, 650 | Max 652 s = 10.87 min | Recomputed, consistent |
| 0.5.2 baseline: 9–14 min, 43/43 | Find the 43-citation run | Only `2026-09-24-lit-ferrylane-openai_gpt-5.6-terra.jsonl` has 43 citations; it is labeled `feynman_version: 0.5.0` | **Metadata mismatch / unverified label** |
| "44 citations" means 44 claims | Read `extractIds` | Map dedupes by ID; 44 distinct IDs, not 44 inline citation instances | Clarified; release wording is broader than the metric |
| 0.5.3 runs are reproducible from a SHA | Read `git_dirty` | All four 0.5.3 rows have `git_dirty: true`; 14/22 rows overall are dirty | **Not reproducible from the recorded SHA alone** |
| Cost | Read `usage.cost_usd` | All 22 rows are `$0`; no `cost` block in the example `models.json` | **Unmeasured** |
| Search benchmark: 7/9 vs 2/9 seminal papers | Look for the benchmark in the repo | No benchmark file or result artifact; only the release note | **Unverified** |

Two further facts matter for reading the claim:

- **The eval is not currently a gate.** Since the last eval commit (`e2bcb84`, 2026-09-24), 46 substantive commits touched `prompts/`, `.feynman/agents/`, `skills/`, or `extensions/` (47 including `.feynman/SYSTEM.md`); 6 touch `prompts/`. A looser count including `package.json` is 110, but 64 of those touch only `package.json` and are mostly version/release metadata. `git log --since=2026-09-25 -- evals` returns 0 commits. No eval result after 2026-09-24 exists in the repo. Either the eval was not run, or it was run and not committed; both violate the README's rule.
- **A concrete missed regression.** Commit `278e9af` (2026-11-05) changed `prompts/lit.md` because a live run improvised `parallel()` and its first workflow call failed. The fix was covered by a prompt-example unit test, not by the research eval. A failed first tool call does not necessarily prevent a final artifact, so `done` would catch this only if the failure prevented the final output; an eval run would at least exercise the path. No post-fix eval result exists.

### What the 0.5.3 numbers do establish

They establish that, on one GPT-5.6 Terra run over four questions, in a dirty worktree, four `/lit` artifacts were produced with a provenance file, every extracted identifier in those four artifacts resolved, and every row's `title_match` was 1 under the 60% heuristic. The pre-wait summaries also record a manual q01 re-score after a transient lookup failure, so `valid` is not a single deterministic pass even in the committed data. That is a real citation-hygiene result. It is not evidence of claim-level accuracy, synthesis quality, or generalization to the other eight questions, other workflows, or other models.

## Remaining issues

### R1 — **MAJOR (F1 residual): §5 says 64 package-only commits; git says 63**
**Location:** §5, “Two further facts matter…”, first bullet.

> “A looser count including `package.json` is 110, but **64 of those touch only `package.json`** and are mostly version/release metadata.”

Per-commit classification of the 110 commits since 2026-09-24 over the six cited paths:

- **63** touch only `package.json` among the six paths;
- **1** touches only `.feynman/SYSTEM.md`;
- **46** touch `prompts/`, `.feynman/agents/`, `skills/`, or `extensions/` (13 of those also touch `package.json`);
- **1** of the 110 is a merge commit (`f57b849`, PR #300, touching `extensions/`).

So the correct partitions are **63 + 47 = 110** (including `SYSTEM.md`) or **63 + 46 + 1 = 110**. The report’s **46 + 64 = 110** works only by folding the `SYSTEM.md`-only commit into the package-only bucket. `git-stats.txt` also records `only_package_json_among_six_paths: 64`, which appears to be the same 110−46 subtraction rather than a measured count. Fix §5 to 63 and make the partition explicit. The headline claim (“46 substantive”) is otherwise correct and no longer presents 110 as substantive churn.

Secondary residuals in the same finding: (a) the 110 still includes one merge commit, so “110 commits” double-counts PR #300 unless non-merge (109) is stated; (b) 13 of the 46 substantive commits also touch `package.json`, so “46 substantive + 63 package-only” is not a clean two-bucket partition of the 46.

### R2 — **MINOR/MAJOR (additional, not among the prior 10): “No benchmark file” for the 7/9 search benchmark is false**
**Location:** §5 release-claim table, last row.

> “Search benchmark: 7/9 vs 2/9 seminal papers | Look for the benchmark in the repo | **No benchmark file or result artifact; only the release note** | Unverified”

The six queries and their nine key papers are in `evals/questions.jsonl`: `q01`–`q06` have 1+2+2+1+2+1 = 9 key papers, and `evals/README.md:61` explicitly calls `q01`–`q06` “the six queries from Feynman's paper-discovery search benchmark.” The repo therefore contains the benchmark inputs; what is missing is the **7/9 vs 2/9 result artifact**. The table should say “benchmark inputs in `evals/questions.jsonl`; no result artifact for the 7/9 comparison.” This also contradicts §2’s own statement that q01–q06 are the paper-discovery search benchmark. `feynman-harness-eval-quality.provenance.md` repeats the “no benchmark file in repo” claim.

### R3 — **MINOR (evidence traceability): fixture score rows have no case IDs and are not in report order**
`fixtures.jsonl` rows carry only `id: q01` and an absolute `workdir`; the case name is only inferable from the path. The rows are in dict order **f1, f2, f3, f4, f5, f7, f8, f6**, while the report table lists f1…f8 with **f6 before f7**. A reader matching table order to raw rows would swap f6 and f7. The f7 row is row **6**, not row 7. Add a `case` field or reorder the table to match. This does not affect the f7 isolation result itself.

### R4 — **MINOR: “All four 0.5.3 rows” is ambiguous**
There are **six** 0.5.3 rows (Terra 4 + Opus 2), and all six are `git_dirty: true`; the report’s “All four 0.5.3 rows” is true for Terra but reads as all 0.5.3 rows. Say “all four Terra 0.5.3 rows” or “all six 0.5.3 rows.” No numeric contradiction, because every 0.5.3 row is dirty.

# Second-pass verification: `outputs/feynman-harness-eval-quality.md`

**Reviewer role:** evidence-integrity audit (second pass, after `notes/feynman-eval-quality-review.md`)
**Target:** `/work/outputs/feynman-harness-eval-quality.md`
**Pinned source:** `/tmp/feynman-src` @ `11744290758648c2ecd7c0d6389cdca9ae580290` (package 0.5.69)
**Rule followed:** report not rewritten; this note is the only authored artifact.

**Verdict:** **9 of 10 prior findings are resolved.** **F1 is only partially resolved:** the headline now uses the defensible 46-commit substantive count, but §5 says **64** commits touch only `package.json`; the git count is **63**. The stated 46+64 arithmetic also silently drops the one `.feynman/SYSTEM.md`-only commit, and the 110 still includes one merge commit. One additional factual error remains in the §5 release-claim table (the search benchmark file). f7 isolation, the probe command, and the 46/110 totals otherwise reproduce.

---

## Prior findings: pass/fail

| ID | Prior finding | Status | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F1** | 110 presented as substantive churn; no decomposition | ❌ **PARTIAL / FAIL** | 110 total ✅; 46 four-path substantive ✅; 47 including `.feynman/SYSTEM.md` ✅; 6 prompt commits ✅; **63 package-only, not 64** ❌; 1 merge (`f57b849`) still undisclosed; 46 includes that merge. See R1. |
| **F2** | “47 … alone” off by one | ✅ Resolved | `git log --since=2026-09-24 -- prompts .feynman/agents skills extensions | wc -l` = 46; adding `.feynman/SYSTEM.md` = 47. Report now states both correctly. |
| **F3** | Determinism “Strong” omitted network-dependent `valid` and manual q01 re-score | ✅ Resolved | §2 caveat cites `run.mjs:183` and `README.md:48`; §3 splits “Scoring logic determinism” (Strong) from “Measurement stability” (Adequate). Both pre-wait summaries say “q01 citation validity was re-scored after a transient lookup failure.” |
| **F4** | f7 fixture confounded by exact key-paper title | ✅ Resolved | Fixture body is now `Test-time compute scaling (Snell et al.) 2408.03314.` — no exact key-paper title. Re-ran `--rescore`: f7 row has `cites: 0`, `valid: null`, `title: null`, `recall: 1`. Recall can only come from the bare-ID substring. |
| **F5** | “4 questions per run” false for one run | ✅ Resolved | Row counts are 4, 4, 2, 4, 4, 4. The 0.5.3 Opus run has 2 rows (q01, q10); its `.md` says only non-biology questions were run because Opus 5.5 refuses q04/q07. Report now says “2–4 questions per run (one Opus run has 2…).” |
| **F6** | §9 “committed results cannot tell” overstated | ✅ Resolved | `2026-09-24-lit-0.5.3-ferrylane_claude-opus-5-5.md:3` documents the q04/q07 refusals; Terra’s 0.5.3 `.md` has no panel explanation. Report now says Opus is explained, Terra is not. |
| **F7** | Probe command did not match recorded command | ✅ Resolved | `probe-result.txt` command is `env -u PI_SESSION_ID -u PI_SESSION_FILE FEYNMAN_TELEMETRY=off timeout 240 feynman --no-session --prompt '…'`. Report shows the same env assignments, timeout, flags, and prompt text; only single-vs-double quote style and line wrapping differ. |
| **F8** | README line 5 cited for `tests/` absence | ✅ Resolved | `evals/README.md:5` supports only `evals/`; `package.json.files` omits both `evals/` and `tests/`. Report now says exactly that. |
| **F9** | `done` described as catching an arbitrary failed workflow call | ✅ Resolved | Report now says `done` catches the failure only if it prevents the final artifact, and an eval run would at least exercise the path. |
| **F10** | “Eight fixtures found four false-positive modes” oversold | ✅ Resolved | Report now says several documented limits were confirmed, one undocumented title-heuristic false positive (`f5`), and one extraction inconsistency (`f7`). |

---

## Remaining issues

### R1 — **MAJOR (F1 residual): §5 says 64 package-only commits; git says 63**
**Location:** §5, “Two further facts matter…”, first bullet.

> “A looser count including `package.json` is 110, but **64 of those touch only `package.json`** and are mostly version/release metadata.”

Per-commit classification of the 110 commits since 2026-09-24 over the six cited paths:

- **63** touch only `package.json` among the six paths;
- **1** touches only `.feynman/SYSTEM.md`;
- **46** touch `prompts/`, `.feynman/agents/`, `skills/`, or `extensions/` (13 of those also touch `package.json`);
- **1** of the 110 is a merge commit (`f57b849`, PR #300, touching `extensions/`).

So the correct partitions are **63 + 47 = 110** (including `SYSTEM.md`) or **63 + 46 + 1 = 110**. The report’s **46 + 64 = 110** works only by folding the `SYSTEM.md`-only commit into the package-only bucket. `git-stats.txt` also records `only_package_json_among_six_paths: 64`, which appears to be the same 110−46 subtraction rather than a measured count. Fix §5 to 63 and make the partition explicit. The headline claim (“46 substantive”) is otherwise correct and no longer presents 110 as substantive churn.

Secondary residuals in the same finding: (a) the 110 still includes one merge commit, so “110 commits” double-counts PR #300 unless non-merge (109) is stated; (b) 13 of the 46 substantive commits also touch `package.json`, so “46 substantive + 63 package-only” is not a clean two-bucket partition of the 46.

### R2 — **MINOR/MAJOR (additional, not among the prior 10): “No benchmark file” for the 7/9 search benchmark is false**
**Location:** §5 release-claim table, last row.

> “Search benchmark: 7/9 vs 2/9 seminal papers | Look for the benchmark in the repo | **No benchmark file or result artifact; only the release note** | Unverified”

The six queries and their nine key papers are in `evals/questions.jsonl`: `q01`–`q06` have 1+2+2+1+2+1 = 9 key papers, and `evals/README.md:61` explicitly calls `q01`–`q06` “the six queries from Feynman's paper-discovery search benchmark.” The repo therefore contains the benchmark inputs; what is missing is the **7/9 vs 2/9 result artifact**. The table should say “benchmark inputs in `evals/questions.jsonl`; no result artifact for the 7/9 comparison.” This also contradicts §2’s own statement that q01–q06 are the paper-discovery search benchmark. `feynman-harness-eval-quality.provenance.md` repeats the “no benchmark file in repo” claim.

### R3 — **MINOR (evidence traceability): fixture score rows have no case IDs and are not in report order**
`fixtures.jsonl` rows carry only `id: q01` and an absolute `workdir`; the case name is only inferable from the path. The rows are in dict order **f1, f2, f3, f4, f5, f7, f8, f6**, while the report table lists f1…f8 with **f6 before f7**. A reader matching table order to raw rows would swap f6 and f7. The f7 row is row **6**, not row 7. Add a `case` field or reorder the table to match. This does not affect the f7 isolation result itself.

### R4 — **MINOR: “All four 0.5.3 rows” is ambiguous**
There are **six** 0.5.3 rows (Terra 4 + Opus 2), and all six are `git_dirty: true`; the report’s “All four 0.5.3 rows” is true for Terra but reads as all 0.5.3 rows. Say “all four Terra 0.5.3 rows” or “all six 0.5.3 rows.” No numeric contradiction, because every 0.5.3 row is dirty.

content.text:
17:- **pi-subagents 0.88.0.** A child waiting for your answer no longer runs out its `timeoutMs` while it waits, and a reply cut off at the model's output limit now fails instead of passing as a success. The subagent widget and `status` show the latest progress a running child reported. Copies of the parent session written by forked subagents are now deleted after `artifactConfig.cleanupDays`, so they no longer fill the disk. Also fixes Windows machines that block PowerShell and gateways that require a prompt cache key.
301:  - pi-subagents: when a subagent's result wakes the main session, that turn keeps its normal system prompt (subagent list, MCP servers, other extensions) and the provider's prompt cache. A per-tool timeout now names the tool instead of a run deadline that never fired.
319:- **A timed-out paper search no longer ends a research step.** A Semantic Scholar or OpenAlex topic search that hits the 25 s timeout is answered from the other index, and other sources say which one did not respond instead of "This operation was aborted".
384:- **The Windows installer no longer fails on slow networks (#309).** When usage telemetry could not reach PostHog quickly, the PostHog library printed a timeout to stderr, and Windows PowerShell treats stderr from the installer's `feynman --help` check as a failure. Each telemetry send now has a 1.5 s budget and ends quietly, so no command waits on telemetry (on a stalled network `feynman --help` took 11 s and printed two errors; it now takes about 2 s and prints nothing). The installers also run their checks with telemetry off and judge them by exit code.
625:- Source-checkout runtime archive rebuilds now use the same fifteen-minute process budget as exact locked runtime restores, avoiding premature timeouts on slow clean environments while retaining the existing transactional exact-lock checks.
629:- Added workflow and runtime regressions that bind Windows native extraction and source-archive rebuilding to their supported timeout contracts.
650:- Timed-out model-tool and user-shell policy handlers still allow later policy handlers to run, then fail closed. User-shell interception returns an explicit non-executing result, so both TUI and RPC paths do not run the command after a policy timeout.
660:- Added executable extension-handler deadline coverage for downstream progress, timeout reporting, expired contexts, late rejection handling, fail-closed TUI/RPC user-shell interception, cumulative dialog timing, parent cancellation, project trust, and tool permission dialogs.
773:- Added an exact timeout regression and retained fail-closed lock, package-graph, and post-install verification.
825:- Updated `posthog-node` to `5.50.0`, including fixes for queue flushing, response-body timeouts, compression memory growth, shutdown, and telemetry value serialization.
74:  - Stopping, interrupting or resuming a research subagent can no longer act on the wrong run: an interrupt with no id is refused, and resuming a worktree child while it is still cleaning up no longer runs it in your main checkout.
117:  - "The model refused to complete the request" says the model declined, and to rephrase or pick another model.
165:  - When a provider stops a subagent with an error such as a content-filter refusal, the error now includes the provider's reply, so a refusal can be told apart from an outage.
196:- **pi-web-access 0.40.0.** Asking about a YouTube or local video works again when a thumbnail comes back with the transcript, excerpts no longer cut an emoji in half, and a new opt-in setting (`fetchContent.redirects: "same-origin"`) refuses redirects to another site.
221:- **An expired sign-in no longer looks like no model.** Feynman treated a ChatGPT, Claude or Copilot sign-in whose short-lived access token had expired as if no model were set up. `feynman` reopened the setup menu, and since 0.5.36 `feynman -p` refused to run. Pi renews the token on the next request, so Feynman now leaves that to Pi and asks you to sign in again only when renewal really fails.
289:- **Pi 1.1.0.** Claude browser login no longer fails with "localhost refused to connect" when port 53692 is reserved or in use (common with Hyper-V/WSL on Windows); it falls back to a free port. "Servers are busy" provider errors and Mistral stream errors are retried instead of ending the turn, fewer requests fail on context limits, and session costs count long prompts correctly. Adds Claude Haiku 5.5; Feynman's default for Anthropic stays Claude Opus.
343:- **Settings saved by Windows Notepad or PowerShell no longer stop Feynman.** Both can save UTF-8 with a byte-order mark, which JSON parsing rejects, so Feynman refused to start with "Invalid Feynman settings ... expected a JSON object", and other commands read the file as empty. Feynman now ignores the mark in `settings.json`, `auth.json`, and `web-search.json`, as Pi does. A settings file with a real JSON error now names the error, for example a trailing comma, instead of the generic message.
484:- Claude Opus 5.5 refuses some biology literature reviews (for example `/lit CRISPR base editing`) with "The model refused to complete the request". The same topics run on GPT-5.6 Terra.
1473:- Installing a new Feynman release on an unsupported (too new) Node version no longer aborts the install and silently pins you to the old version (#177). The version gate still refuses to run and explains what to install, but the package itself updates so the fix is in place once you switch Node versions.
1628:- Clarified that Hugging Face file reads refuse obvious model weights, archives, and dataset shards before download.

content.text:
## Bottom line

Feynman ships a genuinely useful evaluation scaffold: isolated homes and workspaces, a deterministic citation scorer with no LLM judge, per-question wall/token accounting, committed result files, and unusually candid release notes about refusals and known issues. That scaffolding is worth keeping.

But the eval is a **citation-hygiene smoke test, not a research-quality benchmark**. Committed results cover only four of its twelve questions, only `/lit` has results, and the typical run is one pass over four questions with no repeats or uncertainty estimates. Its four headline metrics measure filename existence (`done`), identifier resolvability (`valid`), a 60% title-token overlap heuristic (`title`), and string presence of one or two expected papers (`recall`). None measures whether a cited source supports the claim attached to it.

A short synthetic-artifact probe makes the gap concrete. A one-sentence hand-written report with a correct citation and a minimal provenance file scores **100% on `done`, `valid`, `title`, and `recall`** without running any research workflow. A report claiming a **1000% accuracy improvement** passes the same four metrics. A correct title attached to a fabricated arXiv ID still gets **100% recall**. A key paper listed only under "Rejected sources" also gets **100% recall**. These are not accusations that the committed model runs contain such errors; they show what the metric cannot distinguish.

No committed eval result exists after 2026-09-24, even though the eval's own rule says to run it before and after any prompt, tool, extension, or Pi-version change. In that window, 46 commits touched prompts, agents, skills, or extensions (including one merge); the other 64 are 63 package-only commits and one `SYSTEM.md`-only commit. That window includes a November 5 fix to the `/lit` prompt after a live workflow failure, and **zero commits touched `evals/`**. The rule is well written but not operationalized in CI.

**Verdict:** strong harness engineering, thin measurement, decayed operating discipline. The eval is a useful regression smoke test for citation formatting. It is not yet evidence that Feynman produces trustworthy research, and its 100% results should not be read as capability claims.

---

=== 89-103 ===
### What is genuinely good

These are not consolation prizes; they are the parts a serious eval needs.

- **Isolation.** A fresh home and workspace per question means a run cannot read the developer's real `~/.feynman` or another question's artifacts.
- **Deterministic scoring logic.** The scorer is a readable ~300-line Node script with no LLM judge. Given the same artifact text and the same lookup outcomes, the score is the same. The caveat is `valid`: a failed arXiv/Crossref lookup is removed from both numerator and denominator (`run.mjs:183`; `README.md:48`), and the pre-wait result summaries note that q01 was re-scored after a transient lookup failure. Read `valid` as conditional on lookup success and check `citations` against `citations_checked`.
- **Failure accounting.** `exit_code`, `timed_out`, `completed`, `key_missing`, and error rows are recorded. A timed-out 45-minute run is not silently dropped.
- **Raw evidence design.** Each row points to a workdir intended to contain the full workspace, session JSONL, and `feynman.log`, and `--rescore` can re-score without rerunning the model.
- **Epistemic hygiene in the docs.** The README says "treat a single run as noisy," tells readers to inspect listed failures rather than only percentages, fixes the question set for comparability, and commits both before/after runs. The release notes disclose model refusals and known issues.
- **Privacy.** Eval homes are isolated, telemetry is disabled, and provider keys are read from the environment rather than written into the isolated home.

That is a better foundation than a leaderboard with an opaque judge. The problem is what was built on top of it.

---

=== 173-200 ===
## 5. Release-claim audit

The most specific public claim is in `RELEASES.md` for v0.5.3 (2026-09-24):

> "On the `/lit` eval with GPT-5.6 Terra, 4 of 4 questions finished, all 44 citations resolved with matching titles, and each question ran the researcher, verifier, and reviewer in under 11 minutes (0.5.2: 9-14 minutes, 43 of 43 citations)."

| Claim | Check | Result | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 of 4 questions finished | Read the 0.5.3 Terra JSONL | 4/4 `completed: true` | Recomputed, consistent |
| 44 citations | Sum `citations` across q01/q04/q07/q10 | 11 + 11 + 7 + 15 = 44 distinct identifiers | Recomputed, consistent |
| All 44 resolved | `citations_checked` = 44; all `citation_validity` = 1 | 44/44 | Recomputed, consistent |
| `valid` is artifact-only | Read `run.mjs:183` and the pre-wait summaries | Network-failed lookups are dropped from the denominator; q01 was manually re-scored after a transient failure | **Conditional on lookup success** |
| Matching titles | Every row's `title_match` = 1 | All rows pass the 60% heuristic; the denominator is resolved IDs with a known title, not necessarily all 44 | Recomputed, but heuristic-dependent |
| Under 11 minutes each | `wall_s` = 652, 628, 578, 650 | Max 652 s = 10.87 min | Recomputed, consistent |
| 0.5.2 baseline: 9–14 min, 43/43 | Find the 43-citation run | Only `2026-09-24-lit-ferrylane-openai_gpt-5.6-terra.jsonl` has 43 citations; it is labeled `feynman_version: 0.5.0` | **Metadata mismatch / unverified label** |
| "44 citations" means 44 claims | Read `extractIds` | Map dedupes by ID; 44 distinct IDs, not 44 inline citation instances | Clarified; release wording is broader than the metric |
| 0.5.3 runs are reproducible from a SHA | Read `git_dirty` | All six 0.5.3 rows (four Terra, two Opus) have `git_dirty: true`; 14/22 rows overall are dirty | **Not reproducible from the recorded SHA alone** |
| Cost | Read `usage.cost_usd` | All 22 rows are `$0`; no `cost` block in the example `models.json` | **Unmeasured** |
| Search benchmark: 7/9 vs 2/9 seminal papers | Look for the benchmark inputs/results in the repo | Inputs are in `evals/questions.jsonl` (q01–q06, 9 key papers); no committed result artifact for the 7/9 comparison | **Inputs present; comparison unverified** |

Two further facts matter for reading the claim:

- **The eval is not currently a gate.** Since the last eval commit (`e2bcb84`, 2026-09-24), 46 commits touched `prompts/`, `.feynman/agents/`, `skills/`, or `extensions/` (including one merge), one touched only `.feynman/SYSTEM.md`, and 63 touched only `package.json` (mostly version/release metadata); 6 of the 46 touch `prompts/`. `git log --since=2026-09-25 -- evals` returns 0 commits. No eval result after 2026-09-24 exists in the repo. Either the eval was not run, or it was run and not committed; both violate the README's rule.
- **A concrete missed regression.** Commit `278e9af` (2026-11-05) changed `prompts/lit.md` because a live run improvised `parallel()` and its first workflow call failed. The fix was covered by a prompt-example unit test, not by the research eval. A failed first tool call does not necessarily prevent a final artifact, so `done` would catch this only if the failure prevented the final output; an eval run would at least exercise the path. No post-fix eval result exists.

### What the 0.5.3 numbers do establish

They establish that, on one GPT-5.6 Terra run over four questions, in a dirty worktree, four `/lit` artifacts were produced with a provenance file, every extracted identifier in those four artifacts resolved, and every row's `title_match` was 1 under the 60% heuristic. The pre-wait summaries also record a manual q01 re-score after a transient lookup failure, so `valid` is not a single deterministic pass even in the committed data. That is a real citation-hygiene result. It is not evidence of claim-level accuracy, synthesis quality, or generalization to the other eight questions, other workflows, or other models.
=== 208-238 ===
## 6. Dogfooding notes

I ran this audit from inside a Feynman session and also exercised the installed CLI as a subprocess.

**Live one-shot probe.** In a fresh workspace:

```sh
env -u PI_SESSION_ID -u PI_SESSION_FILE FEYNMAN_TELEMETRY=off timeout 240 \
  feynman --no-session --prompt \
  "Create the file outputs/probe-artifact.md with exactly one line: FEYNMAN_PROBE_OK. Use the write tool, then reply DONE."
```

Result: exit 0, stdout `DONE`, artifact `FEYNMAN_PROBE_OK` (17 bytes). The run also left `outputs/.plans/`, `outputs/.drafts/`, `notes/`, and `papers/` in the workspace. Log: `experiments/feynman-harness-probe/probe.log`; result summary: `probe-result.txt`. This is a small positive data point: the one-shot path exits, writes the requested artifact, and scaffolds the expected workspace.

**What helped the audit.**

- The system prompt's evidence/integrity rules are unusually explicit: separate observation from inference, label blocked/unverified work, verify artifacts on disk, never invent results. Those rules directly shaped this report.
- Shell access plus a source-first workflow made it possible to audit the evaluator's code, not just its marketing. Many agent products make this impossible because only a hosted API is exposed.
- The harness's own conventions (slugged artifacts, provenance sidecars, raw logs) are good habits for any eval.

**Frictions observed.**

- **The eval is not shipped.** `evals/` is absent from the npm package (`evals/README.md:5`); `tests/` is also absent from `package.json` `files`. An installed user cannot run the harness's own eval without cloning the repo. That is a transparency cost.
- **There is no `feynman eval` command.** Running the eval means building the repo, supplying a `models.json`, exporting a provider key, and choosing ids/workflow manually. That is developer-only, which helps explain why the rule decays.
- **`--rescore` depends on author-local state.** Every committed row stores an absolute `workdir` (`/Users/advaitpaliwal/.cache/...` or `/var/folders/...`). The artifacts are not committed. A fresh clone cannot rescore any published result.
- **Version and model skew.** The installed harness is 0.5.65; the source snapshot is 0.5.69. The committed evals use GPT-5.6 Terra / Claude Opus 5.5 / Claude Sonnet 5; this session runs DeepSeek v4.1 Flash. I can audit the scorer and the claims, but not reproduce the model behavior.
- **The summary row hides denominators.** `table()` takes the unweighted mean of per-question percentages, excluding nulls (`run.mjs:251-259`). A run with 3/4 completion can show `valid 100%` because the failed question is null and dropped, while `recall` includes the failure as 0 (see `2026-09-24-lit-0.5.3-pre-wait-ferrylane-openai_gpt-5.6-terra.jsonl`). The columns have different denominators. That is visible if you read carefully, but the "all" row encourages a single number.
- **Self-evaluation bias.** I am the harness. There is no independent human rater in this loop. The quantitative claims here trace to files and commands; the ratings are judgments and should be treated as such.

---

content.text:
Done. The case study is at:

- **`outputs/feynman-harness-eval-quality.md`** — canonical report
- `outputs/feynman-harness-eval-quality.provenance.md` — source/verification sidecar
- `experiments/feynman-eval-audit/` — fixtures, scorer probe, git stats, release-claim recomputation
- `experiments/feynman-harness-probe/` — live one-shot CLI probe
- `notes/feynman-eval-quality-review*.md` — two adversarial reviewer passes

### What I found

**The good:** Feynman’s eval is real infrastructure, not a vibe check. Fresh `FEYNMAN_HOME` and workspace per question, deterministic scorer with no LLM judge, per-question wall/token accounting, committed result files, raw workdirs for rescoring, and candid docs about noise and refusals.

**The core limitation:** it measures citation *hygiene*, not research quality. The four headline metrics are:

| Metric | What it actually checks |
|---|---|
| `done` | A final `.md` and matching `.provenance.md` exist |
| `valid` | Cited IDs resolve via arXiv/Crossref/doi.org |
| `title` | ≥60% of resolved title tokens appear on a line containing the ID |
| `recall` | An expected paper’s ID or exact title appears *anywhere* |

None checks whether the cited source supports the claim attached to it.

**Meta-eval result:** I wrote eight synthetic artifacts and ran the repo’s own `--rescore` scorer. A one-sentence artifact with a correct citation and a minimal provenance file scored **100% on `done`, `valid`, `title`, and `recall`** without any research workflow. A **1000% accuracy claim** passed all four metrics. A fabricated arXiv ID still got **100% recall** because the exact title was present. A key paper listed only under “Rejected sources” also got **100% recall**. A wrong bracketed title passed because the surrounding prose supplied enough title tokens. These are scorer limitations, not accusations about the committed model runs.

**Release claims:** the v0.5.3 “4/4 questions, 44/44 citations resolved” claim recomputes correctly from the JSONL: 11+11+7+15 = 44 distinct IDs, all valid, max wall 652 s. But “44 citations” means 44 distinct identifiers, not 44 supported claims; the 0.5.3 Terra run was on a dirty worktree; all 22 committed rows show `$0` because no cost block is configured; and the 7/9 search-benchmark comparison has inputs in `questions.jsonl` but no committed result artifact.

**Process:** no eval result has been committed since 2026-09-24. Since then, 46 commits touched prompts/agents/skills/extensions (plus 63 package-only and one SYSTEM-only commit), and zero touched `evals/`. The November 5 `/lit` prompt fix — made after a live workflow failure — had no post-fix eval. The README’s “run before/after any prompt/tool/Pi change” rule is not operationalized in CI.

### Top recommendations

1. Make the scorer itself testable: importable module + `tests/eval-scorer.test.ts` with adversarial fixtures; run in CI.
2. Persist a small artifact bundle per run so `--rescore` works from a fresh clone, and replace absolute `workdir` paths.
3. Separate `artifact_present` / `provenance_present` / `verifier_ran` / `reviewer_ran` from quality metrics; add a claim-level audit sample.
4. Run 2–3 repeats or at least two independent runs before claiming “100%”; report n and uncertainty.
5. Add post-cutoff and no-tools controls before interpreting canonical-paper recall as retrieval skill.

**Limitations:** I did not rerun `/lit` end-to-end; the eval’s gateway/models aren’t reproducible here, and the installed model differs (DeepSeek v4.1 Flash vs GPT-5.6 Terra/Claude Opus 5.5). The report’s quantitative claims trace to the pinned repo and local artifacts; the scorecard ratings are judgments, not measurements. Two reviewer subagent passes caught and corrected an inflated commit count and a missing network-denominator caveat before delivery.
